The flow speed in the second section is given by \(v = Q/A\), where \(Q = 9.5 \, \text{L/s} = 0.0095 \, \text{m}^3/\text{s}\) and \(A = \pi (0.02 \, \text{m})^2\). This yields \(v \approx 7.6 \, \text{m/s}\) (2 significant figures).

The centripetal acceleration is \(a = 4\pi^2 r / T^2 = 4\pi^2 (5.0) / (4.0)^2 = 5\pi^2/4 \approx 12 \, \text{m/s}^2\) (2 significant figures).

The gravitational force is \(F = G m_1 m_2 / r^2 = (6.67 \times 10^{-11}) (0.0100)(0.500) / (0.0500)^2 = 1.334 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N}\). Thus \(X = 1.33\).

The semi-major axis from Kepler's third law: \(a = a_{\text{Earth}} (T/T_{\text{Earth}})^{2/3}\). Using \(a_{\text{Earth}} = 1.496 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m}\) and \(T = 4.62 \, \text{years}\), we get \(a = 4.15 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m}\), so the value in units of \(10^{11} \, \text{m}\) is \(4.15\).

ANSWER: 7.6,12,1.33,4.15
